newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end up 1.44 pct on tax merger plan.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end up 1.44 pct on tax merger plan.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed sharply higher on Friday after the cabinet on Thursday approved a "two-into-one" tax merger plan to boost the island's investment and economy, brokers said.

The cabinet agreed to merge the island's two income taxes into one business income tax and set the merged rate at 25 percent, seen effective from 1998. The move would avoid double taxation and help corporate structures, officials said.
The index once surged to as high as 9,804.20 points, and ended at 9,770.80, a gain of 138.46 points or 1.44 percent.
Turnover was modest at T$139.5 billion.
Electronics surged 2.45 percent partly reflecting Wall Street's and Nasdaq's overnight gains, brokers said.

The tax merger would reduce tax revenues by about T$30-40 billion a year, but the finance ministry would recoup the sharp downturn by assessing a 10 percent levy on profits that enterprises reserve rather than distribute to shareholders immediately, officials said.
Brokers said the planned 10 percent levy on companies' retained earnings will force those with high retained earnings to issue higher stock dividends in 1998 to avoid double taxation.

Michael Hung, independent analyst: "If parliament approves the proposal, companies with high retained earnings like Taiwan Semiconductor are expected to issue higher stock dividends in 1998 to avoid double taxation, a move that will benefit general investors."
Microchip giant Taiwan Semiconductor rose the daily seven percent limit to T$152. Glass giant Taiwan Glass rose T$2.1 to T$47.2. Both have high retained earnings.
Brokers also attributed Friday's rise to loosening liquidity after the central bank repeatedly injected funds into the banking system in recent sessions.
"In addition to tax merger plan and Wall Street's gains, the central bank's fund injections effectively helped the upward momentum," said Nomura Securities analyst Amy Huang.

Computer giant Acer surged T$4 to T$88.5 on the Economic Daily News report that it had received US$1 billion in orders from International Business Machines Corp, although an Acer spokeswoman declined to comment.
Brokers said they expected the index to rise further on Saturday, seeing a 9,700-9,850 range.
